reconciled_candidates.label: Bandwidth Problem and Backtracking
reconciled_candidates.description: Defines the bandwidth optimization problem: given a graph, find a linear ordering of vertices that minimizes the maximum length of an edge. A naive solution enumerates all n! permutations and checks the maximum edge span. Backtracking can prune the search by comparing against the current best bandwidth.
coverage_criteria: Student can state the bandwidth problem and compute bandwidth for a small example.
Student can explain why a brute-force search over all permutations is inefficient and that it is NP-hard.

reconciled_candidates.merge_rationale: These candidates together cover the problem definition, contest context, and backtracking application for the bandwidth problem.
